chain.label: Pilots fatigued from long duty day and early wakeup
chain.trigger: it had been more than 15 hours since the pilots' last significant sleep period, and they had been on duty for 14 1/2 hours

chain.label: Night operation
chain.trigger: Night instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) prevailed for the flight

chain.label: Low ceiling and reduced visibility at Kirksville
chain.trigger: ceiling overcast at 300 feet agl... visibility 4 statute miles (sm) in mist

chain.label: FAA regulation permits descent below MDA on approach lights alone
chain.trigger: current Federal Aviation Regulations that allow pilots to descend below the MDA into a region in which safe obstacle clearance is not assured based upon seeing only the airport approach lights

chain.label: Pilots violated sterile cockpit rule and omitted required approach callouts
chain.trigger: the pilots' conversation after the airplane descended below 10,000 feet msl...was not consistent with these sterile cockpit procedures; the first officer did not make the required '100 above minimums' or 'minimums' callouts

caused_by.evidence: the pilots' unprofessional behavior during the flight and their fatigue likely contributed to their degraded performance

chain.label: Captain continued descent below MDA without required visual cues, unmoderated to impact
chain.trigger: the pilots continued their 1,200 fpm descent below the MDA without an appropriate visual reference

caused_by.evidence: the low ceiling and reduced visibility at IRK made the nonprecision approach more challenging

these regulations can have the unintended effect of encouraging some pilots to descend below the MDA in an attempt to acquire visual cues that will permit them to continue the approach, as occurred in this case
these factors may also have detracted from the pilots' adherence to company standard procedures and callouts
the captain made a risky decision to continue the approach based on inadequate visual cues... consistent with the degrading effects of fatigue

chain.label: First officer failed to challenge captain; division-of-duties breakdown
chain.trigger: their failure to adhere to the established division of duties between the flying and nonflying (monitoring) pilot

caused_by.evidence: the first officer did not challenge the captain's failure to level off at or reduce the airplane's rate of descent around the MDA, despite the fact that the first officer did not see any ground references
his failure to monitor and react to the captain's deviations from nonprecision approach procedures was consistent with the degrading effects (slowed reactions and/or tunnel vision) of fatigue

chain.label: Aircraft struck trees and crashed short of the runway
chain.trigger: struck trees on final approach and crashed short of runway 36 at the Kirksville Regional Airport (IRK)

caused_by.evidence: descent below the minimum descent altitude (MDA) before required visual cues were available (which continued unmoderated until the airplane struck the trees)
failure to adhere to the established division of duties between the flying and nonflying (monitoring) pilot

chain.label: Fatal and serious injuries to occupants
chain.trigger: The captain, first officer, and 11 of the 13 passengers were fatally injured, and 2 passengers received serious injuries.

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by impact and a postimpact fire.
